declarations.en: For commutative rings $R,S,T$, with $R$- and $S$-algebra structures on $T$, assume that $T$ is formally unramified over $S$. No $R$-algebra structure on $S$ or scalar-tower compatibility is assumed here. For every $R$-derivation $D:T\to T$, if $D(\iota(s))=0$ for all $s\in S$, where $\iota:S\to T$ is the structure map, then $D$ is the zero derivation.

declarations.en: Write $\mathbb Q(t)$ for the intermediate field generated by $t$. For a characteristic-zero field $F$, $\partial_t$ denotes the specified $\mathbb Q$-derivation $F\to F$: if $t$ is transcendental over $\mathbb Q$ and $F/\mathbb Q(t)$ is algebraic, it is the formally étale extension of the derivation $p(t)\mapsto p\prime(t)$ on $\mathbb Q[t]$; otherwise it is the zero derivation. Scalar multiplication $a\partial_t$ means pointwise multiplication by $a$. A place $P$ of $F$ means a valuation subring $O_P\ne F$ containing every rational scalar, with no restriction to an affine chart. If $F$ is a curve field, meaning that it is finite dimensional over $\mathbb Q(z)$ for some transcendental $z$, then $v_P(f)=-\log(V_P(f))\in\mathbb Z$, where $V_P$ is the valuation of the maximal ideal of the discrete valuation ring $O_P$. This is a total function, with $v_P(0)=0$. The symbol $\pi_P$ is the chosen element of $F$ with $v_P(\pi_P)=1$. The canonical multiplicative valuation of an arbitrary valuation subring $O$ is denoted by $\nu_O$. Let $K$ be a characteristic-zero field, let $t\in K$ be transcendental over $\mathbb Q$, and assume $K/\mathbb Q(t)$ is algebraic. Then $\partial_t(t)=1$.

declarations.ja: $\mathbb Q(t)$ は $t$ が生成する中間体を表す。標数零の体 $F$ に対し、$\partial_t$ は指定された $\mathbb Q$-導分 $F\to F$ を表す。$t$ が $\mathbb Q$ 上超越的で $F/\mathbb Q(t)$ が代数拡大であるとき、これは $\mathbb Q[t]$ 上の導分 $p(t)\mapsto p\prime(t)$ の形式的エタール延長であり、それ以外では零導分である。$a\partial_t$ は各値に $a$ を掛けることを意味する。$F$ の素点 $P$ とは、すべての有理数のスカラーを含み $F$ と異なる付値部分環 $O_P$ であり、特定のアフィン座標近傍への制限はない。曲線体とは、ある超越元 $z$ に対し $F$ が $\mathbb Q(z)$ 上有限次元となる体である。このとき $v_P(f)=-\log(V_P(f))\in\mathbb Z$ とし、$V_P$ は離散付値環 $O_P$ の極大イデアルから得られる付値である。これは全域関数であり、$v_P(0)=0$ である。$\pi_P$ は $v_P(\pi_P)=1$ を満たす選ばれた $F$ の元である。任意の付値部分環 $O$ の標準的な乗法的付値を $\nu_O$ と書く。 $K$ を標数零の体、$t\in K$ を $\mathbb Q$ 上超越的な元とし、$K/\mathbb Q(t)$ は代数拡大であると仮定する。このとき $\partial_t(t)=1$ である。

declarations.en: Write $\mathbb Q(t)$ for the intermediate field generated by $t$. For a characteristic-zero field $F$, $\partial_t$ denotes the specified $\mathbb Q$-derivation $F\to F$: if $t$ is transcendental over $\mathbb Q$ and $F/\mathbb Q(t)$ is algebraic, it is the formally étale extension of the derivation $p(t)\mapsto p\prime(t)$ on $\mathbb Q[t]$; otherwise it is the zero derivation. Scalar multiplication $a\partial_t$ means pointwise multiplication by $a$. A place $P$ of $F$ means a valuation subring $O_P\ne F$ containing every rational scalar, with no restriction to an affine chart. If $F$ is a curve field, meaning that it is finite dimensional over $\mathbb Q(z)$ for some transcendental $z$, then $v_P(f)=-\log(V_P(f))\in\mathbb Z$, where $V_P$ is the valuation of the maximal ideal of the discrete valuation ring $O_P$. This is a total function, with $v_P(0)=0$. The symbol $\pi_P$ is the chosen element of $F$ with $v_P(\pi_P)=1$. The canonical multiplicative valuation of an arbitrary valuation subring $O$ is denoted by $\nu_O$. Let $K$ be a characteristic-zero field, let $t\in K$ be transcendental over $\mathbb Q$, and assume $K/\mathbb Q(t)$ is algebraic. For every $s\in K$, with no transcendence or algebraicity assumption on $s$, equality of derivations $\partial_s=\partial_s(t)\partial_t$ holds, that is, $\partial_s(x)=\partial_s(t)\partial_t(x)$ for all $x\in K$.

declarations.en:
Write $\mathbb Q(t)$ for the intermediate field generated by $t$. For a characteristic-zero field $F$, $\partial_t$ denotes the specified $\mathbb Q$-derivation $F	o F$: if $t$ is transcendental over $\mathbb Q$ and $F/\mathbb Q(t)$ is algebraic, it is the formally étale extension of the derivation $p(t)\mapsto p\prime(t)$ on $\mathbb Q[t]$; otherwise it is the zero derivation. Scalar multiplication $a\partial_t$ means pointwise multiplication by $a$. A place $P$ of $F$ means a valuation subring $O_P
e F$ containing every rational scalar, with no restriction to an affine chart. If $F$ is a curve field, meaning that it is finite dimensional over $\mathbb Q(z)$ for some transcendental $z$, then $v_P(f)=-\log(V_P(f))\in\mathbb Z$, where $V_P$ is the valuation of the maximal ideal of the discrete valuation ring $O_P$. This is a total function, with $v_P(0)=0$. The symbol $\pi_P$ is the chosen element of $F$ with $v_P(\pi_P)=1$. The canonical multiplicative valuation of an arbitrary valuation subring $O$ is denoted by $
u_O$. Let $N\in\mathbb N$ and let $M$ consist of an intermediate field $F\subseteq\overline{\mathbb Q(T)}$ over $\mathbb Q$, elements $u,v\in F$ with $u$ transcendental, $u^N+v^N=1$, $\mathbb Q(u,v)=F$, and $[F:\mathbb Q(u)]=N<\infty$. No separate positivity bound on $N$ is imposed. The hypothesis $h_{m DVR}$ says that $O_P$ is a discrete valuation ring for every place $P$. Write $o_P(f)$ for the integer order obtained from this supplied discrete-valuation-ring structure; its definition is the same negative logarithm of the maximal-ideal valuation and gives $o_P(0)=0$. Define the integer $e_P(f)$ by $e_P(f)=o_P(m_{ ar f}(f))$ when $f\in O_P$, where $ ar f$ is its residue and $m_{ ar f}\in\mathbb Q[X]$ is its minimal polynomial; when $f
otin O_P$, define $e_P(f)=-o_P(f)$. These are integer indices, with no natural-number truncation. Places range over all the valuation subrings just specified, including those outside an affine chart. For every $\psi\in F$ transcendental over $\mathbb Q$, every place $P$, and a proof that $\psi\in O_P$, install the curve-field structure supplied by $M$. Then \[v_P(\partial_{\pi_P}(\psi))=e_P(\psi)-1.\]
